Lyndon B. Johnson

Project 42 · presidential suite · from templates-president/johnson.json · index · repo randomcase/lyndon-b-johnson

Democratic · 1963–1969 · the American standard: president 3 of the four who managed the war

Role. Oversaw the massive escalation: the Tonkin Gulf resolution, Rolling Thunder, the first Marines at Da Nang, and over 500,000 combat troops in country by 1968. Announced a partial bombing halt and his own withdrawal from the 1968 race on the same night.

Decisions, one line item each

1963-11-26NSAM 273, four days after Dallas: the objective is to help Saigon win; the withdrawal plan is quietly dropped.
1964-08-07Tonkin Gulf resolution passes 416–0 and 88–2 after an attack on 2 August and a second on 4 August that the NSA's own history says did not happen.
1965-02-13Rolling Thunder approved; sustained bombing of the North begins 2 March.
1965-03-083,500 Marines land at Da Nang to guard the air base: the first combat units.
1965-07-28'We will stand in Vietnam': 50,000 more troops announced at a midday press conference, 125,000 in all, with more to follow; no reserve call-up, no declaration, no tax.
1966-1967Westmoreland's requests approved in steps to 525,000; the war of attrition and the body count.
1968-01-30Tet. Militarily repelled; politically decisive.
1968-03-25The Wise Men, reconvened, tell him to disengage. Clifford, new at Defense, agrees.
1968-03-31Announces a bombing halt north of the 20th parallel, talks, and that he will not seek re-election.
1968-10-31Full bombing halt; Paris talks expand. Nixon's campaign, through Anna Chennault, urges Saigon to stall.

The Joint Chiefs, with their president

Chiefs in office during the term. A chief carried over from the previous president is listed once, with the earlier president, and given nothing more here — only the duty he owed this one, and, where it applies, his last days with him. The Joint Staff, the Pentagon, Arlington, Virginia. The Chairman’s office is on the E-ring, second floor, river side; the Chiefs meet in the “Tank”, Room 2E924, and from 1972 in the Gold Room next to it.
